title: If upgrading to jammy on a Raspberry Pi, check for the presence of the broken "match" section of the yaml config. This was present in the default config for Raspberry Pi images dating back to focal.
commit_message: If upgrading to jammy on a Raspberry Pi, check for the presence of the broken "match" section of the yaml config. This was present in the default config for Raspberry Pi images dating back to focal.

diff --git a/DistUpgrade/DistUpgradeQuirks.py b/DistUpgrade/DistUpgradeQuirks.py

--- a/DistUpgrade/DistUpgradeQuirks.py

@@ -151,6 +151,7 @@ class DistUpgradeQuirks(object):
         if 'linux-firmware-raspi2' in cache:

     # individual quirks handler when the dpkg run is finished ---------

@@ -1377,3 +1378,62 @@ class DistUpgradeQuirks(object):
         except IOError as exc:
             logging.error("unable to write new boot config to %s: %s; %s",
                           boot_config_filename, exc, failure_action)
+
+    def _remove_netplan_match_rpi(self, netplan_dir='/etc/netplan'):
+        failure_action = (
+            "You may need to manually edit your netplan config "
+            "and remove the line \"driver: bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx\". "
+            "See LP: #1970761 for further details")
+
+        try:
+            import yaml
+        except ImportError:
+            logging.error("failed to import yaml library. %s", failure_action)
+            return
+
+        for netplan_config_file in glob.glob("%s/*.yaml" % netplan_dir):
+            try:
+                netplan_config_filename = os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                                                       netplan_config_file)
+                with open(netplan_config_filename, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                    orig_content = f.read()
+                    netplan_yaml = yaml.load(orig_content,
+                                             Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)
+
+            except FileNotFoundError:
+                logging.error("failed to open netplan configuration in %s; %s",
+                              netplan_config_filename, failure_action)
+                return
+
+            file_modified = False
+            try:
+                for eth in netplan_yaml["network"]["ethernets"].values():
+                    if eth["match"]["driver"] == "bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx":
+                        file_modified = True
+                        del eth["match"]
+                        if "set-name" in eth:
+                            del eth["set-name"]
+            except KeyError:
+                continue
+
+            if not file_modified:
+                continue
+
+            try:
+                netplan_backup_filename = (netplan_config_filename +
+                                           '.distUpgrade')
+                with open(netplan_backup_filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                    f.write(orig_content)
+            except IOError as exc:
+                logging.error("unable to write netplan config backup to "
+                              "%s: %s; %s",
+                              netplan_backup_filename, exc, failure_action)
+                return
+            try:
+                with open(netplan_config_filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+                    yaml.dump(netplan_yaml, f, default_flow_style=False)
+            except IOError as exc:
+                logging.error("unable to write new netplan config to "
+                              "%s: %s; %s",
+                              netplan_config_filename, exc, failure_action)
+                return
diff --git a/debian/changelog b/debian/changelog

--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,11 @@
+ubuntu-release-upgrader (1:22.04.11) jammy; urgency=medium
+
+  * DistUpgrade/DistUpgradeQuirks.py: Remove section of netplan
+    config that is installed by default on Raspberry Pi and
+    causes netplan failures after upgrade to jammy (LP: #1970761)
+
+ -- William 'jawn-smith' Wilson <jawn-smith@ubuntu.com>  Tue, 03 May 2022 12:54:45 -0500
+

 from DistUpgrade.DistUpgradeQuirks import DistUpgradeQuirks

             with open(os.path.join(boot_dir, 'config.txt')) as f:
                 self.assertTrue(f.read() == expected_config_txt)
 
+    # This test case tests the scenario where the invalid
+    # match section is present and needs to be removed
+    def test_remove_netplan_match_single_removal(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as netplan_dir:
+            config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    # this is a test comment to ensure it is preserved in the backup
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      # this section will be deleted
+      match:
+        driver: bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx
+        name: en*
+      optional: true
+      set-name: eth0
+  wifis:
+    wlan0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      access-points:
+        "TestWifi":
+          password: "TestPassword"
+  version: 2
+"""
+            expected_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      optional: true
+  wifis:
+    wlan0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      access-points:
+        "TestWifi":
+          password: "TestPassword"
+  version: 2
+"""
+            config_filename = '99-test-netplan.yaml'
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, config_filename), 'w') as f:
+                f.write(config_yaml)
+
+            mock_controller = mock.Mock()
+            q = DistUpgradeQuirks(mock_controller, mock.Mock())
+            q._remove_netplan_match_rpi(netplan_dir)
+
+            # make sure the backup exists and is the same as the original
+            backup_config_filename = config_filename + '.distUpgrade'
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, backup_config_filename)))
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      backup_config_filename)) as f:
+                self.assertTrue(f.read() == config_yaml)
+
+            # make sure the new contents are what we expect
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, config_filename)) as f:
+                new_config = yaml.load(f, yaml.SafeLoader)
+                expected_config = yaml.load(expected_config_yaml,
+                                            yaml.SafeLoader)
+                self.assertTrue(new_config == expected_config)
+
+    # This test case tests the scenario where the match
+    # section is present but is valid syntax
+    def test_remove_netplan_match_valid_syntax(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as netplan_dir:
+            config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      match:
+        # this is a test comment to ensure it is preserved in the backup
+        driver: ["bcmgenet", "smsc95xx", "lan78xx"]
+      optional: true
+      set-name: eth0
+  wifis:
+    wlan0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      access-points:
+        "TestWifi":
+          password: "TestPassword"
+  version: 2
+"""
+
+            mock_controller = mock.Mock()
+            q = DistUpgradeQuirks(mock_controller, mock.Mock())
+            q._remove_netplan_match_rpi(netplan_dir)
+
+            self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, '50-cloud-init.yaml.distUpgrade')))
+
+    # This test case tests the scenario where the match
+    # section not present at all
+    def test_remove_netplan_match_no_match(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as netplan_dir:
+            config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      optional: true
+  wifis:
+    wlan0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      access-points:
+        "TestWifi":
+          password: "TestPassword"
+    version: 2
+"""
+
+            mock_controller = mock.Mock()
+            q = DistUpgradeQuirks(mock_controller, mock.Mock())
+            q._remove_netplan_match_rpi(netplan_dir)
+
+            self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, '50-cloud-init.yaml.distUpgrade')))
+
+    # This test case tests the scenario where the invalid
+    # match section is present in one file, but multiple
+    # config files exist
+    def test_remove_netplan_match_one_of_multiple(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as netplan_dir:
+            ethernet_config_yaml = """\
+############
+# also
+# test
+# multi
+# line
+# comments
+# are
+# preserved
+############
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      match:
+        driver: bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx
+      optional: true
+      set-name: eth0
+  version: 2
+"""
+            wifi_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  wifis:
+    wlan0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      access-points:
+        "TestWifi":
+          password: "TestPassword"
+  version: 2
+"""
+            expected_ethernet_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      optional: true
+  version: 2
+"""
+            e_config_filename = '01-test-ethernet.yaml'
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, e_config_filename), 'w') as f:
+                f.write(ethernet_config_yaml)
+
+            w_config_filename = '02-test-wifi.yaml'
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, w_config_filename), 'w') as f:
+                f.write(wifi_config_yaml)
+
+            mock_controller = mock.Mock()
+            q = DistUpgradeQuirks(mock_controller, mock.Mock())
+            q._remove_netplan_match_rpi(netplan_dir)
+
+            # make sure the backup exists and is the same as the original
+            backup_config_filename = e_config_filename + '.distUpgrade'
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, backup_config_filename)))
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      backup_config_filename)) as f:
+                self.assertTrue(f.read() == ethernet_config_yaml)
+
+            # make sure the new contents are what we expect
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, e_config_filename)) as f:
+                new_config = yaml.load(f, yaml.SafeLoader)
+                expected_config = yaml.load(expected_ethernet_config_yaml,
+                                            yaml.SafeLoader)
+                self.assertTrue(new_config == expected_config)
+
+            # make sure a backup wasn't created for the config
+            # that doesn't need modification
+            self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, w_config_filename + '.distUpgrade')))
+
+    # This test case tests the scenario where the invalid
+    # match section is present in multiple files
+    def test_remove_netplan_match_multiple(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as netplan_dir:
+            eth0_config_yaml = """\
+# comments can go at the top
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      match:
+        driver: bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx
+      optional: true
+      set-name: eth0
+  version: 2
+"""
+            eth1_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth1:
+      dhcp4: true
+      match:
+        driver: bcmgenet smsc95xx lan78xx
+  version: 2
+# comments can go at the bottom too
+"""
+            expected_eth0_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth0:
+      dhcp4: true
+      optional: true
+  version: 2
+"""
+            expected_eth1_config_yaml = """\
+network:
+  ethernets:
+    eth1:
+      dhcp4: true
+  version: 2
+"""
+            eth0_config_filename = '01-test-eth0.yaml'
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      eth0_config_filename), 'w') as f:
+                f.write(eth0_config_yaml)
+
+            eth1_config_filename = '02-test-eth1.yaml'
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      eth1_config_filename), 'w') as f:
+                f.write(eth1_config_yaml)
+
+            mock_controller = mock.Mock()
+            q = DistUpgradeQuirks(mock_controller, mock.Mock())
+            q._remove_netplan_match_rpi(netplan_dir)
+
+            # make sure the backup exists and is the same as the original
+            backup_eth0_filename = eth0_config_filename + '.distUpgrade'
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, backup_eth0_filename)))
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      backup_eth0_filename)) as f:
+                self.assertTrue(f.read() == eth0_config_yaml)
+
+            # make sure the modified contents are what we expect
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, eth0_config_filename)) as f:
+                new_config = yaml.load(f, yaml.SafeLoader)
+                expected_config = yaml.load(expected_eth0_config_yaml,
+                                            yaml.SafeLoader)
+                self.assertTrue(new_config == expected_config)
+
+            # make sure the backup exists and is the same as the original
+            backup_eth1_filename = eth1_config_filename + '.distUpgrade'
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(
+                netplan_dir, backup_eth1_filename)))
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir,
+                      backup_eth1_filename)) as f:
+                self.assertTrue(f.read() == eth1_config_yaml)
+
+            # make sure the modified contents are what we expect
+            with open(os.path.join(netplan_dir, eth1_config_filename)) as f:
+                new_config = yaml.load(f, yaml.SafeLoader)
+                expected_config = yaml.load(expected_eth1_config_yaml,
+                                            yaml.SafeLoader)
+                self.assertTrue(new_config == expected_config)
+
 
 class TestSnapQuirks(unittest.TestCase):
